title: On one GOES scale, isolated active regions gave equal M-flare rates per unit of magnetic flux in Solar Cycles 23-25 (MDI and HMI, 1998-2026); the Cycle 25 excess is in 2024 multi-region complexes
abstract: Question: on one GOES X-ray flux scale, does one relation between active-region magnetic flux and M-flare rate hold for Solar Cycles 23, 24 and 25, and where is the remaining Cycle 25 excess? Method: we joined SOHO/MDI SMARP (1996-2010) and SDO/HMI SHARP (2010-2026) active-region patches through the line-of-sight flux keyword USFLUXL, calibrated in the 2010 overlap (HMI = 0.795 x MDI, 0.76-0.82). We modelled 5,304 true-scale M1+ flares on 9,421 days (1998-06 to 2026-10) as the sum of patch rates with one factor per cycle, and we predicted each cycle from the other two. Intervals come from a 27-day block bootstrap. Results: at matched patch flux, Cycle 23/Cycle 24 is 0.89 (0.73-1.16) and Cycle 25/Cycle 24 is 1.16 (0.92-1.43). Held-out observed/predicted ratios are 0.77, 0.95 and 1.24, against 0.64/0.90/1.57 for sunspot number, 0.73/1.21/1.15 for F10.7 and 0.94/0.75/1.43 for SWPC region classes. For M5+ flares the patch-flux ratios are 0.86 and 0.94. Patches with one NOAA region flare at the same rate per unit flux in all cycles (C23/C24 0.99, 0.76-1.35; C25/C24 1.08, 0.82-1.48). Multi-region patches give 0.84 (0.61-1.35) in Cycle 23 and 1.53 (1.12-2.41) in Cycle 25, although Cycle 23 had as much flux in such complexes (45%) as Cycle 25 (47%; Cycle 24 29%). Without 2024 the Cycle 25 complex ratio is 1.16 (0.82-1.83). At matched HMI flux, Cycle 25 complexes have the same R, current helicity, free-energy proxy and shear as Cycle 24 complexes (ratios 0.99-1.04); with these parameters, flux growth and patch age in the model, the complex excess stays at 1.49-1.59. Limitations: the overlap has no patch above 3e22 Mx and an F10.7 check suggests the MDI scale can be 10% high, so C23/C24 is 0.77-1.02 over a plus or minus 10% calibration range; MDI and HMI segment complexes differently; Cycle 25 is incomplete; the complex excess depends mainly on one year.

display.caption: (a) Cycle 23/Cycle 24 and Cycle 25/Cycle 24 M1+ rate ratios at matched normalization, true GOES scale, 1998-06 to 2026-10, with 95% 27-day block-bootstrap intervals (200 replicates). (b) Observed/predicted M1+ flares of each cycle when the model is fitted on the other two cycles. The calibrated MDI+HMI line-of-sight patch flux gives the most uniform held-out ratios.

(a) M1+ rate relative to Cycle 24 at matched patch flux, for patches with one NOAA region and with two or more. Single-region patches agree in all three cycles; Cycle 25 multi-region patches flare 1.53 times more. (b) Share of disk patch flux in multi-region patches by year (MDI to 2010-04, HMI after). (c) HMI era: the Cycle 25/Cycle 24 multi-patch excess stays when R, TOTUSJH, TOTPOT, ABSNJZH, SAVNCPP and MEANSHR enter the model, and these parameters are equal in both cycles at matched flux (diamonds).

Year-by-year M1+ yield factor (mean of Cycle 24 active years = 1) at matched sunspot number, matched SRS regions and matched LOS patch flux, years with at least 20 M1+ flares. At matched patch flux only 2024 (1.49, 1.13-1.94) is above all Cycle 24 years.

citations.reason: We use its true-scale (homogeneous) flare list and NCEI detection counts; our results agree with its Cycle 25 flare rate per F10.7 unit.

We reuse its SRS region tables, flare-to-region table and region-sum model code, extend its HMI analysis to Cycle 23 with MDI, and confirm its multi-region-complex result; we show that the complex excess is specific to Cycle 25 and mostly to 2024.
